title: Defining Structs and Creating Objects
learningObjectives: Define a struct and create instances of the custom type.
Initialize fields and access them through objects.
Distinguish type definition from object creation.
Group related values into one record.
Choose simple record types for appropriate data.

understand.concept: A struct defines a custom type grouping related data members. A variable of that type is an object with its own member values.
understand.whyItMatters: Grouping related fields models records such as a point, product or student.
understand.explain: Define a type, create objects, and use the dot operator to access members.

examples.title: Define Point
examples.explanation: Point groups two coordinates in a named type.

examples.title: Create separate objects
examples.explanation: Each object has its own member value.

examples.title: Use custom type
examples.code: struct Pair{int first;int second;};\nPair p{5,9};int sum=p.first+p.second;
examples.explanation: Members can be used in ordinary expressions.

practise.guidedTask: For Defining Structs and Creating Objects, trace every example. List each type, object, member, initial value, access path, and state change. Identify where encapsulation or initialization affects correctness.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ model focused on Defining Structs and Creating Objects (such as a Point, Student, Product, or Account). Include multiple objects, initialization, at least one operation/member access, and test normal, boundary and invalid states. Explain which fields should be public or private and why.
hints: Define the type and its responsibilities before creating objects.
Initialize members deliberately and trace their values.
Use dot for objects and arrow only for pointers.
Keep fields private when they must enforce rules.
Test object creation, valid operations and rejected updates.

questions.explanation: A struct defines a grouped data type.
Each object has its own state.
Dot accesses a member on an object.
Members may have different declared types.
A structured type groups related fields.
